text: Investigating the required-flag bug in src/click/core.py now.

In `src/click/_unicodefun.py` (`_verify_python_env`), the lookup is wrapped in `try/except Exception`, and the except branch sets `fs_enc = "ascii"` (line 13). Because the very next check is `if fs_enc != "ascii": return`, that fallback deliberately makes click abort with the "Python was configured to use ASCII as encoding for the environment" RuntimeError rather than silently continuing with an unknown encoding.

`RuntimeError` — `_verify_python_env` ends with `raise RuntimeError("\n\n".join(extra))`, whose message begins "Click will abort further execution because Python was configured to use ASCII as encoding for the environment. Consult https://click.palletsprojects.com/unicode-support/ for mitigation steps."
Still working on the required-flag bug in src/click/core.py (diagnosis + minimal fix + full-suite verification).
Still working on the echo-with-no-streams bug (_compat.py / _termui_impl.py / utils.py).

Fixed. Root cause: in `Option.__init__` (src/click/core.py:2519) the implicit flag default was assigned unconditionally — `if is_flag and default_is_missing: self.default = False` — so a required flag got `default=False`, `value_is_missing(False)` was False, and `MissingParameter` was never raised. Restored the `and not self.required` guard. Now `@click.option('--foo', is_flag=True, required=True)` invoked without `--foo` exits 2 with "Error: Missing option '--foo'."; non-required flags, `flag_value`, `multiple`, `count` and `--foo/--no-foo` cases all still behave correctly, and the full suite is unchanged: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.
Working on the envvar + flag_value bug in src/click/core.py.
From `click.utils` — `src/click/__init__.py` does `from .utils import echo` (alongside `format_filename`, `get_app_dir`, `get_binary_stream`, `get_text_stream`, `open_file`).

`TypeError` — `style` wraps `_interpret_color(fg)` in `try/except KeyError` and re-raises `TypeError(f"Unknown color {fg!r}")` (termui.py:580-584; the `bg` branch does the same with `bg!r`). Calling `_interpret_color` directly raises `KeyError` instead.
On it now (urgent): fixing the cls-preservation bug in src/click/decorators.py.
Fixed and verified (see earlier message): `Option.__init__` in src/click/core.py now keeps `default=None` for required flags, so omitting a required flag raises "Missing option".
Still in progress: echo-with-no-streams fix across _compat.py / _termui_impl.py / utils.py.
Still in progress: envvar + flag_value bug in src/click/core.py.
Still in progress (urgent): cls-preservation bug in src/click/decorators.py.

`_join_param_hints` (exceptions.py:14-20) returns `" / ".join(repr(x) for x in param_hint)` — each item repr'd (so strings get quoted) and joined with `" / "`. E.g. `['--foo', '--bar']` → `"'--foo' / '--bar'"`. `None` and plain strings are returned unchanged.

In `BadParameter.format_message`, when both `param_hint` and `self.param` are None it returns `_("Invalid value: {message}").format(message=self.message)` (exceptions.py:119-120) — i.e. `"Invalid value: <message>"`, without the "for ..." part.

`click.exceptions.Abort` (i.e. `click.Abort`) — with no message and no args. In `prompt`'s inner `prompt_func`, the read is wrapped in `try/except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError): ... raise Abort()` (termui.py:144-150); the docstring states the same ("If the user aborts the input by sending a interrupt signal, this function will catch it and raise a :exc:`Abort` exception"). `Abort` is a bare `RuntimeError` subclass, deliberately not a `UsageError`; `confirm()` does the same.
Working on the symlink-resolution bug in src/click/types.py.

Fixed. `argument()`'s decorator popped `cls` out of the closure-shared `attrs` dict, so reusing the same `@click.argument(..., cls=X)` decorator object (or applying it twice) silently fell back to the default `Argument` for every application after the first. It now copies the attrs first (`argument_attrs = attrs.copy()`), mirroring the existing fix for `option()` (#926). Verified: reused `@click.argument(cls=MyArg)` keeps MyArg on every command, argument order/parsing unchanged, `@click.command(cls=...)`/`group`/`pass_context` unaffected, full suite still 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.

It returns the `color` argument unchanged (`if color is not None: return color`, globals.py:61-62). Only when `color is None` does it fall back to the current context's `ctx.color` (or `None` if there is no context).
`None` — with `silent=True` the `LookupError` from the context stack is caught and `None` is returned; without it, `RuntimeError("There is no active click context.")` is raised.
Working on the flag default_map bug in src/click/core.py.
`"8.0.1"` — `__version__ = "8.0.1"` in src/click/__init__.py.
Fixed and verified: required flags now raise "Missing option" (Option.__init__ guard restored in src/click/core.py).
Fixed and verified: echo/progressbar/pager no longer crash when there are no standard streams (None-handling restored in _compat.py, _termui_impl.py, utils.py).
Fixed and verified: envvar-provided values for flag_value options (see src/click/core.py change).
Fixed and verified: reused @click.argument(cls=...) decorators now preserve cls (src/click/decorators.py).
Correction: the envvar + flag_value fix in src/click/core.py is still being verified — not yet done. ETA ~6 min.

`TypeError("Cannot have two nargs < 0")` — parser.py:92-94 (`elif nargs < 0:` → `if spos is not None: raise TypeError("Cannot have two nargs < 0")`). A single negative value is legal (it marks the wildcard position).
